match.reason: No bank point teaches all three turnover indicators (inventory, receivables and payables turnover in days); the closest card, Efficiency ratios, covers only receivable turnover alongside an expense ratio and is a broader Business Studies card, while the two credit-sales and credit-purchases cards teach the balances but not turnover.

draft.title: Turnover indicators
card: Inventory turnover
shows how many days, on average, stock sits before it is sold. It compares average inventory with cost of sales, then converts the result to days.
Receivables turnover
shows how many days, on average, customers take to pay what they owe. It compares average accounts receivable with credit sales, then converts the result to days.
Payables turnover
shows how many days, on average, the business takes to pay its suppliers. It compares average accounts payable with credit purchases, then converts the result to days.

Each result is in days. A business wants stock sold and customers paying quickly. Taking longer to pay suppliers keeps cash in the business for longer, but a very long time may harm supplier relationships.
draft.remember: Each turnover indicator counts days: stock held, customers paying and the business paying.

a.q: A business reports that its accounts receivable turnover rose from 30 days to 45 days. What does this show?
opts: Customers are taking longer to pay the business
Customers are paying the business more quickly
The business is taking longer to pay its suppliers
Stock is sitting in the store for longer before sale
a.why: Accounts receivable turnover counts the days customers take to pay. A rise from 30 to 45 days means customers are slower. Stock days belong to inventory turnover, and the days the business takes to pay belong to payables turnover.
a.clue: Receivables are money owed by customers.

b.q: Harbour Hardware in Geelong has an inventory turnover of 40 days last year and 55 days this year. What is the most likely meaning?
opts: Stock is taking longer to sell than it did last year
Stock is selling faster than it did last year
The business is paying its suppliers more slowly
Customers are taking longer to pay their accounts
b.why: Inventory turnover in days shows how long stock sits before it is sold. A rise from 40 to 55 days means stock is sitting longer, so it sells more slowly. Fewer days would mean faster sales, so the second option reverses the change.
b.clue: A higher number of days means stock waits longer.

a.best: Customers are taking longer to pay the business

b.best: Stock is taking longer to sell than it did last year

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'the second option reverses the change', but options are shuffled. In this order the second option is the correct answer, so the explanation points at the wrong option. Name the option by its wording ('Stock is selling faster'), not its position.
The clue 'A higher number of days means stock waits longer' all but states the correct option, so a student can answer without understanding the indicator.
Tense mismatch: 'has an inventory turnover of 40 days last year'. Should be 'had ... last year and has ... this year'.

check.summary: The card and answers are correct. Why (b) refers to 'the second option' by position, which after shuffling is the correct answer, so it contradicts the question. Question b's clue nearly gives the answer away, and its stem has a tense error.
